prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the incretin hormone GLP-1, its physiology and its active peptide form, which made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B041 prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Round 1 did not weaken the scientific case. The chain runs from incretin physiology and proglucagon processing, through identification of the biologically active truncated GLP-1, to degradation-resistant agonists whose benefit is confirmed in large independent outcome trials on glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints. The mechanism is stable, the work is original and mature, and the clinical scale exceeds any other shortlisted candidate. A prize anchored on the hormone and its active form keeps the citation on discovery, which is what this prize is for, and uses exactly three names without cutting anyone from a second part.
statement.case_against: The weakness is attribution, and the chair is right that every member names it. Priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is contested, Habener and other early contributors are outside the credited names, and Knudsen's acylated analogue programme is decisive for patients yet falls outside the trio. A discovery prize that omits the drug-development step may look incomplete, and I cannot adjudicate the priority history from the permitted files. I also accept that long-term safety data on chronic incretin therapy are still accumulating, although I do not think that affects the core discovery.

responses.point: Sandberg moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to the Mojsov trio but still regards Knudsen's long-acting analogue step as a distinct, decisive achievement and not a late detail.
responses.response: I accept that characterisation and do not call Knudsen's step minor; liraglutide and semaglutide are why the biology reached patients. Our disagreement is about what the citation should reward. The active-peptide identification is the hinge between hormone physiology and any drug design, whereas the analogue programme is a separate, industrial achievement with its own credit structure. I would not add her as a fourth name, and I would not make the citation vague enough to imply she is honoured. If the committee decided to reward the drug step, the honest route is to replace Mojsov, and I would then want that argued explicitly on the record. I do not currently think the argument wins.

responses.point: The chair asks whether the committee will adjudicate the Mojsov and Habener priority record, and what evidence would change a member's position on the third laureate.
responses.response: I cannot adjudicate it from the permitted files, so I will not claim to. My position is conditional. If a documented record showed that Mojsov's identification of the active truncated peptide was not independent or not first, I would move to Habener or to Knudsen, but only on documented facts, not on recollection or reputation. Without such evidence, the converging view of all six openings is the better working assumption, and a contested claim argues for care in wording, not for exclusion. The citation should name the active peptide form and not state who was first.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranks TNF blockade (Feldmann and Maini) second as a mature, overdue and cleanly attributed bench-to-bedside discovery, and lists B044 among her alternatives.
responses.response: The attribution is as clean as any on the list and I agree it is mature, so I take it seriously. My hesitation is scope. It validated one cytokine as a target in disease, and the antibodies were engineered by others and fall outside the two names. I rank it below CAR-T, which created a new therapeutic modality. I still do not see it competing with B041 this year, and a second part would break the three-person limit. I would keep it as a strong candidate for a later year, particularly if the committee wants a rheumatology-centred recognition.

responses.point: Perlmann prefers the unfolded protein response (Walter and Mori) as his next candidate for its clean attribution and decades of confirmation, and would handle the drug-development step in a later prize.
responses.response: I agree with the cleanliness of the Walter and Mori attribution, and with leaving drug development to a separate decision. Where I differ is on the order of alternatives. The disease links of the unfolded protein response remain largely correlative, with no derived approved therapy, so I put B023 ahead of B011 as the next candidate. Durable remissions in refractory leukaemia and lymphoma are shown. I would not oppose B011 as a later prize, and I accept that a prize for basic cell biology is a legitimate choice if the committee wants to defer clinical validation. I will list B023 first and B011 second on my own alternatives.

responses.point: El-Manira regards the B023 credit question as unresolved because June, Sadelain and Rosenberg represent three different contributions and Eshhar is outside the credited names.
responses.response: That is fair, and it changes how I would frame CAR-T. Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer is a separate lineage from CAR engineering, so a defensible set would more likely be June and Sadelain only, as Perlmann and the chair also suggest, and I would no longer insist on three. Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept remains a real gap that no credited-name choice repairs. I therefore hold CAR-T as the strongest alternative and not a competitor this year. I also take your point that long-term safety of chronic incretin therapy is not fully known, but it bears on dosing and indications and not on the discovery.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide holds against Habener's work, which I cannot verify from the permitted files.
Whether the committee wants the citation to reward hormone physiology and the active peptide only, or also the analogue drug programme.
Whether a defensible CAR-T laureate set exists with Eshhar outside the credited names, and whether Rosenberg belongs in it.
Whether long-term safety data on chronic incretin therapy will change the assessment of impact.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on the shortlist. I disclose the 2016 spatial transcriptomics paper and co-authors Castelo-Branco, Betsholtz, Ernfors, Frisen, Lundeberg and Kharchenko, and prior co-authorship with Sandberg and Frisen, none on a shortlisted topic and none credited. Nothing has changed since round 1, and I do not think recusal is warranted.
